prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: one polished desktop homepage concept image for an unbiased preference survey about the existing LEVNAT / Systems Engineering software consultancy website.
Format: a single landscape 3:2 raster image, ideally 1536 x 1024. Straight-on, pixel-sharp website screenshot, edge-to-edge website canvas. No perspective distortion, no physical laptop/phone frame around the whole image, no collage, no side-by-side variants.
Keep the same content, legible text scale, CTA prominence and visible page depth as the other concepts: top navigation, a strong hero occupying roughly the top 75%, and one clearly visible four-service strip at the bottom. Professional finished visual design with restrained, realistic interface details.
Exact visible English text (render accurately, no additional slogans):
Brand: "LEVNAT", with small descriptor "Systems Engineering".
Navigation: "Services" "Work" "Approach" "Contact".
Headline: "Software that works." on one line and "Support that stays." on the next, using at most three lines in total.
Subtitle: "Web apps, native iOS, integrations and ongoing support."
Main button: "Discuss your project".
Secondary text link: "Explore services".
Bottom four capability labels: "Software development", "iOS & Swift", "Integrations", "Security & support".
Show no made-up client logos, awards, testimonials, team photos, badges of certification, SLA, prices, percentages or charts/metrics. Do not add a style name, letter, recommendation or comparison caption inside the website image. Any tiny product interface text is minimal and generic, not client proof. Keep the offer and main action easy to understand.

Visual direction: refined cyberpunk engineering. Very dark graphite and deep navy surfaces, icy cyan as the single main accent, tiny restrained violet lighting details. Hero composition: spacious editorial copy on the left and a beautiful genuinely volumetric orbital software service system on the right, with one central glass/wireframe sphere connected to a small native-phone shape, a shield and a backend module. Subtle fine 3D ground grid and depth, no rectangular Matrix wall, no full-screen glyph rain, no gaming HUD, no XP, no fake telemetry. Preserve the original site's intriguing 3D DNA while presenting a mature software business. Clean neutral contemporary sans typography, light text. Lower service strip is thin, quiet and organized. Make the cyan CTA as prominent as in the other concepts.

Visual direction: bright product studio. Warm off-white canvas, white surfaces, deep navy type and one confident royal-blue action accent. Airy, inviting and polished, with tactile soft shadows and excellent visual hierarchy. Hero composition: clear copy at left; at right a carefully art-directed cluster of floating, realistic native iOS and web-app interface panels with clean generic lists, forms and navigation. This is a software studio, not a device seller: interfaces sit directly in the website composition with only a slim single native-phone silhouette as part of the hero illustration. No orbital galaxy, no dark/neon scene, no developer terminal. Rounded but disciplined product surfaces and approachable typography. A horizontal four-service strip sits at the bottom with simple meaningful line symbols.

Visual direction: warm Swiss editorial engineering studio. Warm ivory background, almost-black ink, restrained vermilion-orange accent. Sophisticated print-inspired grid, generous negative space, fine rules, strong left alignment, precise large grotesk typography, sharp corners and exceptional text clarity. Hero composition must feel substantially different from a standard SaaS layout: the two-line headline spans a broad upper-left editorial column, with compact subtitle and CTA set on the grid beneath it; an elegant flat 2D technical flow diagram occupies the complementary right column, representing interface to API to data with a few simple geometric modules and thin neutral connectors. No 3D planets, floating device renders, neon, photos or illustrative people. Four bottom service columns use clean typographic numbering and restrained rules, with no invented extra copy. The result should feel like an exacting independent design/engineering practice.

Visual direction: midnight precision engineering, premium and restrained rather than cyberpunk. Near-black/navy monochrome background, soft white typography and a small muted champagne-gold action accent. A centered composition: refined navigation, centered headline and subtitle in the upper hero, CTA directly underneath, and one large beautifully lit sculptural system below/behind the copy with ample clear space around the text. The sculpture is three interlocking precision-machined glass and dark ceramic modules, an abstract software architecture object with a quiet glow and believable materials. No orbital map, no grid of planets, no HUD, no glyphs, no gold coins, no financial/crypto imagery, no excessive metallic decoration. Elegant geometric sans typography, thin neutral dividers. Four capability labels line the bottom in a disciplined understated row. Premium software consulting, not a luxury-product advert.

Visual direction: bold modular product engineering. Light acid-lime and warm pale-gray color blocking, black ink, a single dark charcoal CTA, sharp corners, sturdy clean typography and a memorable graphic layout. A flat, highly practical bento composition rather than a dark dashboard: broad headline and subtitle in the upper left, an immediately clear main CTA, and asymmetrical rectangular product-preview modules to the right and below, with one native app preview, an API connection block and an integration flow. The page should be expressive yet readable and businesslike, not playful clutter or a wall of cards. No 3D galaxy, no shiny sculpture, no gradients, no fake charts, metrics or screenshots full of dense text. Strong black/lime contrast, deliberate negative space, crisp two-dimensional geometry. Four service labels remain equally visible at the bottom and the primary CTA remains as prominent as in the other concepts.
